text:
maya: heads-up — saw a transient tail-latency spike on canary today around 15:12 UTC. started after the 14:58 roll that enabled the new kernel-selector heuristics. looks like microbatch sizes collapsed to 1 for a subset of requests and admission oscillated.

serge: ugh. saw traces? any noisy tenant patterns? :thinking_face:

maya: attaching quick profiler extract and a tiny log snippet below. KV cache hit-rate also dropped on gpu-node-7.

maya: ```
[2026-03-17T15:12:01Z] req=abcd kernel=pref_dense_v2 chosen_confidence=0.12 seq_len=32 microbatch=1 latency_p90=420ms
[2026-03-17T15:12:02Z] kube: admission: accepted=3 rejected=8 backlog=27
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] kvcache: shard=5 hits=12 misses=98 eviction_rate=0.67
```

liam: interesting that kernel-selector confidence is low. new algo picks dense kernels when memory+throughput estimate slightly favors it, but we didn't account for prefix/KV cache effects. when microbatch=1 the overhead kills latency.

eva: can we repro on staging by toggling the selector flag?

maya: i tried a quick flag toggle on staging — similar but smaller magnitude. staging has fewer concurrent prefixes so kvcache hit-rate stayed higher.

serge: sounds like an interaction: kernel selector -> different execution path -> changes memory footprint -> kvcache shard eviction -> admission backpressure -> smaller microbatches -> worse tail. classic emergent behavior.

deploy-bot: deployment maya/kernel-selector-v2 rolled to canary at 2026-03-17T14:58:13Z

liam: i'll run the sampled profiler across the canary cluster and dump the kernel decision distribution and kv-hit timeline. maya, can you collect the admission-controller metrics for the same window? backlog, tokens/sec, accepted rate?

maya: on it. pulling adm logs now, uploading snippet to #eng-runtime-artifacts.

eva: quick mitigation idea: 1) force the selector to prefer previous kernel when prefix_kv_pressure > 0.5; 2) increase min_microbatch to 2 for canary nodes; 3) temporarily pin kernel to legacy path. which is least invasive?

serge: min_microbatch increase is fastest. forcing selector is medium-risk. pinning kernel needs rollback plan. do min_microbatch=2 as quick patch and monitor.

liam: agreed. i'll prepare a hotfix PR to admission controller to set min_microbatch=2 for canary pools and include a metric to track "forced_microbatch" ratio.

maya: after we patch, we should run a narrow canary to validate tail drops. also add an alert: if microbatch=1 proportion > 1% and p90 > 300ms trigger page.

serge: add unit test to kernel selector that simulates kvcache miss surge and ensures selection logic prefers lower-perf kernel that is cache-friendly when kvcache_eviction_rate>0.5.

deploy-bot: hotfix PR opened: https://git.reddemo/infra/pulls/892 (liam)

maya: rolling patch to canary now. will update in ~5m. :eyes:

liam: profiler run shows kernel-choice shifted from ~75% fused_gemm to ~60% pref_dense_v2 during spike window, and microbatch=1 requests jumped from 0.4% -> 4.2%. kv shard-5 became hot due to repeated small-prefix requests from tenant-b.

eva: tenant-b had a recent model switch? could explain prefix skew.

maya: tenant-b rolled a short prompt+tooling change at 14:45. correlates. reaching out to their PM to coordinate rate-limiter/ttl changes.

serge: postmortem action items: (1) short-term: min_microbatch=2 canary + alert; (2) mid-term: kernel-selector feature gate for kvcache-aware heuristics; (3) longer: admission controller smoothing to avoid oscillation when kvcache_eviction spikes.

liam: adding item: sampled tracing for microbatch decision path (add trace_id in logs). helps root-cause future ones.

maya: patch applied to canary. initial numbers look better — p90 down from ~420ms to ~260ms and forced_microbatch metric flipped on for ~2.1% of requests.

eva: great. leave the canary for 2 hours then either rollback or promote with the selector fix.

serge: thanks all. follow-up: schedule a short sync tomorrow to design the kvcache-aware kernel selector and admission smoothing.

maya: noted. I'll file a tracking ticket and include the profiler artifacts.

liam: ticket created: INF-2312. linking traces and logs.

maya: closing loop here — will post the full artifacts and postmortem draft in #postmortems later. :white_check_mark:
